subject: Hosted API pricing — minimum spend, on-demand overage, and burst slabs
messages:
From: Maya Lee <maya@aurumhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — min spend & burst behavior

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Aurum is excited about Redwood's latency and model routing controls. Procurement asked me to get clarifications on two items before we loop legal:

1) Minimum monthly commitment: does Redwood require a monthly minimum for the hosted API, or can we start on pure usage? If there is a minimum, how is it applied to the first invoice and how do true-ups work?

2) Burst / overage pricing: our workload is spiky (seasonal claims processing). If we commit to a baseline and then burst, how are overage tokens billed? Is there a capped multiplier or a sliding slab? Are there any automatic fallbacks to on-demand models with different unit prices?

Can you share a sample invoice or pricing sheet (per-token rates at volume breakpoints) and any standard concession you give for new-enterprise ramp?

Thanks,
Maya
Procurement Manager
Aurum Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Maya Lee <maya@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — min spend & burst behavior

Hi Maya — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. High level answers below, attaching a concise pricing breakdown CSV and an updated proposal workbook for the Aurum use case (see attachments).

1) Minimum monthly commitment: For hosted API we offer two options: pure on-demand (no minimum) and commit tiers. Commits are monthly or annual and act as a floor against usage; any usage below the commit is charged against the commit (no refunds). True-ups are monthly — if you exceed the commit, overage is billed at the agreed overage rate for that tier on the next invoice.

2) Burst / overage pricing: We support a burst buffer on top of commit. By default overage is billed at 1.25x the base per-token rate for the committed tier (this is the hosted default). For large enterprise commits we negotiate a different slab — typically 1.1x for the first 25% overage and 1.4x beyond 100% overage if there is sustained uplift. Alternatively, customers can opt for an on-demand fallback where excess requests route to on-demand capacity at our published on-demand unit price (no multiplier) but with potential differences in latency and routing.

Concessions for first-year ramp: we commonly offer a limited ramp discount (one-time credit or reduced overage multiplier) for the first 3–6 months to smooth onboarding. I'll propose two options in the attached workbook: a standard commit and a ramp-friendly commit.

Attaching: RDW-pricing-breakdown.csv, Aurum_proposal_v3.xlsx

Let me know the procurement team's preference and your expected month-1 baseline vs peak. I can pull together a short mutual action plan (MAP) if you want legal and security loops to start.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurumhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aurumhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — min spend & burst behavior

Karthik — thanks for the overview. A few clarifying Qs from procurement:

- If we pick a commit tier (example: 5M tokens/mo), and in month 2 we spike to 9M tokens, is the 4M overage charged entirely at the multiplier rate, or do we get volume-breakpoint pricing for the extra 4M (i.e., progressive breakpoints like 0–5M, 5–8M, 8M+)?

- Is there a soft-burst allowance (e.g., 10% free burst) for short spikes due to edge cases?

Also, can you attach SOC2 or evidence for security — Legal will require it.

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior Procurement Analyst
Aurum Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurumhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — min spend & burst behavior

Daniel — good questions. Quick answers below and a compact example table embedded in the pricing CSV.

- Progressive slab treatment: overages are billed against the tiered structure (progressive slabs) unless you opt into the simple multiplier overage model. In practice we offer two billing flavors:
  * Slab-style: excess tokens fall into higher-volume breakpoints with their corresponding unit price (so a spike that pushes you into a higher slab will get that slab price only for the tokens in that slab).
  * Multiplier-style: one flat multiplier over the committed tier's base rate for all overage tokens (simpler for forecasting).

- Soft-burst allowance: We can include a 10% soft-burst allowance (free) for spikes under 72 hours if you choose an annual commit. For monthly commits we typically offer a 5% short-window buffer.

Attached: SOC2-cert.pdf (redacted report) and the RDW-pricing-breakdown.csv with illustrative slabs.

If you prefer, we can model three scenarios (baseline, 2x spike, sustained >3 months uplift) and show month-by-month invoices to help procurement decide.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
ben@redwood.com

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurumhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — min spend & burst behavior

Ben / Karthik — that helps. Procurement prefers the slab-style overage (easier to justify) but would like a guaranteed cap on effective unit cost during spikes for budgeting: could Redwood agree to a max effective token price (e.g., not exceed 1.5x base rate) for any monthly billing cycle, assuming spikes are not sustained beyond 30 days?

Also, legal asked whether a one-time onboarding credit could be applied to month 1 to offset higher initial usage while we integrate. Something in the 10–15% of month-1 expected bill would help.

If you can confirm those two concessions we can route to legal and get a draft PO ready.

Thanks,
Daniel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@aurumhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — min spend & burst behavior

Daniel — thanks and appreciate the clarity on procurement's stance. Quick summary and commitment from Redwood:

- Slab-style overage: agreed (we'll bill overage on progressive slabs as in the attached CSV).
- Cap on effective unit cost: we can cap the effective per-token cost at 1.5x the committed base-rate for any monthly cycle so long as the spike is transient (definition: <30 continuous days of >100% over-commit). If spikes persist beyond 30 days we revert to negotiated sustained uplift terms.
- Onboarding credit: we will provide a one-time credit equal to 12% of the expected month-1 bill (applied on the first invoice) for new enterprise commitments >$25k/mo.

Next steps: I'll update the Aurum_proposal_v3.xlsx to mark these concessions and send a DocuSign-ready SLA + MSA. Lauren — can you coordinate legal redlines and prepare the DocuSign envelope (DocuSign-Aurum-SLA.docx)?

Maya / Daniel — if that sounds acceptable I'll route the updated docs today so legal can start review.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
